questions.question: Classify solutions with pH 2, 7, 9 and 13 as acidic, neutral or basic, and state which is the strongest acid and which the strongest base.
questions.expected_answer: pH 2 acidic (strongest acid); pH 7 neutral; pH 9 basic (weak base); pH 13 basic (strongest base).

questions.question: Explain why a solution of pH 3 is not just 'a little' more acidic than one of pH 5.
questions.expected_answer: Each pH step is a factor of ten in hydrogen ion concentration, so pH 3 is 10 × 10 = 100 times more acidic than pH 5.

questions.question: Give two safety rules for working with acids and bases and the reason for each.
questions.expected_answer: Wear safety goggles, because both strong acids and strong bases can damage the eyes. When diluting, add acid to water, never water to acid, because the heat released can make the mixture boil and spit.
